title: Menswear Editorial Content for Catalog
brief:
77 images across 23 clothing SKUs in 9 looks (accessories appear in shots only, no images of their own).
Per SKU: bottoms = front, back, detail, full body; coats and outer tops = cropped front, back, detail; items under the coat = cropped front, back, detail (layer off); tops = one tight cropped front.
2750 × 3500 px, JPG (rendered 3:4, cropped to fit the site), photoreal AI renders.

Who: young menswear customers (B13+) across three profiles, Smart, Urban and Streetwear, 3 looks each, one AI model per look 

Why: a test of whether influencer-style imagery lifts sell-through (ST%) on high-stock seasonal styles that sell weakly online.

Style: candid street style that looks shot on a phone by a friend, in clean, premium Moscow locations (Smart in minimal cafés by day, Urban in courtyards and café fronts, Streetwear at apartment blocks at night). Direct phone flash, close to plain walls, minimal backgrounds. Cool, unimpressed attitude. Gen Z styling with unbranded accessories (sunglasses, watch, tote, coffee).

title: Gloria Jaens Content Brand Guideline
brief:
Top line: a single brand guide that tells anyone producing imagery (photographers, stylists, retouchers, ecommerce, store anyone ) exactly how a shoot should look, so output is consistent across channels and needs fewer rounds of feedback.

What goes into it

Brand look: positioning, mood, keywords, and on-brand vs. off-brand examples
Visual style: lighting, colour and grade, camera angles, composition
People: casting, styling, posing, rules for kids and teens
Product and locations: how product is shown, plus sets, props and backdrops
Shot lists: required shots per use case (e-com, editorial, campaign, video, banners)
Post-production: retouching level, export specs, file naming, delivery
Process: briefing template, approval stages, usage rights and legal
AI imagery: where it’s allowed, perspective and camera rules, review checklist, labelling

What to define first

Scope: which brands, markets and channels
Users: who will actually work from the guide
Format: short PDF, living page, or checklist pack
Reference images: 20-30 on-brand and off-brand examples
Ownership: who writes it, signs it off, and keeps it updated
Success measure: e.g. fewer reshoots, faster approvals
